summary: Model lock eviction observed when latency-mitigation throttle activated during weighted rollout
description: Issue summary: During a staged weighted rollout of gptj-rlhf-v2 for BrightForms (dedicated pool), we observed tenant model locks (model pins) being evicted after the platform activated a latency-mitigation throttle for a short burst of slow inference responses. Impact: Customer experienced mixed model responses (some requests routed to fallback variant) for a subset of sessions for ~18 minutes, causing degraded generation quality for a handful of mid-volume tenants. Environment: prod us-east (dedicated cluster bf-dedicated-03), serving-runtime v1.17.2, orchestrator v2.4.0.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Start weighted rollout: target weight 20% on gptj-rlhf-v2 for route /v1/generate for BrightForms tenant accounts.
2) Simulate transient GPU slowdown on two nodes (reduce available batch slots) or trigger latency-mitigation via synthetic slow model for 5-10s bursts.
3) Observe orchestrator throttle (latency-mitigation) kick in and health smoothing to mark instances as slow.
4) Watch routing logs and pin coherence service for pin eviction events and subsequent fallback routing to legacy variant.
observed_behavior: Pins for affected tenant sessions were evicted shortly after the throttle engaged. Many requests were routed to fallback variant (gptj-rlhf-v1-legacy) despite explicit tenant pin on the new version. Edge logs show affinity token validated but pin removed by orchestrator with reason 'eviction:latency-mitigation'.
expected_behavior: During transient latency mitigation, pinned sessions should remain bound to the pinned model variant. If eviction is unavoidable, orchestrator should emit structured event and trigger immediate redeploy to compatible fallback but preserve pin preference when possible.
logs:
[2026-03-10T14:02:12Z] orchestrator: pin-manager: tenant=brightforms:acct-991 eviction_request={reason: latency-mitigation, trigger: health_smoothing, node: node-12}
[2026-03-10T14:02:12Z] edge-proxy: affinity-validator: tenant=brightforms:acct-991 token=eyJ... validated=true route=/v1/generate model_pin=gptj-rlhf-v2
[2026-03-10T14:02:13Z] router: assign: tenant=brightforms:acct-991 target_model=gptj-rlhf-v1-legacy fallback_reason=pin_evicted
[2026-03-10T14:18:35Z] orchestrator: pin-manager: pin-recreate_attempt tenant=brightforms:acct-991 result=success
investigation_notes:
- Initial hypothesis: orchestrator's latency-mitigation path treats 'pinned' sessions as evictable to reduce tail latency during a node-level slowdown.
- We reproduced locally by toggling health_smoothing thresholds; pin-manager evicts when node health falls below 0.65 and remaining capacity < threshold.
- Edge validated affinity token before eviction; eviction occurs at control-plane pin-manager level, not edge.
- Related PR flagged: orchestrator change in github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/1427 relaxes pin-stability checks during aggressive latency-mitigation.
- Observed correlation with autoscaler preemption events on same cluster around 14:01 UTC — combinational effect: preemption reduced batch slots, triggered health smoothing, then latency-mitigation invoked eviction logic.
- Affected cohort: ~12 tenant sessions across 3 customer accounts, BrightForms highest visible error rate due to pinned heavy inputs.
- No evidence of token corruption or edge cookie issues.
workaround:
1) Temporarily increase health_smoothing threshold on bf-dedicated-03 to 0.55 to avoid early eviction.
2) For immediate customer relief, force re-pin via admin API (POST /admin/pins/restore) for affected sessions.
3) Opened support ticket with BrightForms to re-run affected requests after re-pin.
Note: workaround requires operator with admin perms and will only reduce recurrence window during rollout.
resolution_notes:
Mitigation applied: rolled back orchestrator commit that relaxed pin-stability (reverted PR #1427) in canary subset and changed latency-mitigation to mark pins as protected for pinned sessions on dedicated clusters. Autoscaler preemption tuning applied to reduce simultaneous preemption events.
Planned fix: implement pin-protection flag in pin-manager so latency-mitigation marks 'allow_eviction=false' for pinned session tokens; add telemetry counters for eviction-by-reason.
Follow-up: postmortem scheduled; update runbook to include explicit steps to restore pins and a safe rollback policy for orchestrator changes affecting pinning.
